summary:
We developed a 3D sandbox exploration and challenging game inspired by Terraria and NASA’s Artemis program. Set in the future, the story begins with a young space enthusiast reading historical archives about how humanity established a lunar presence and reached Mars. As the protagonist imagines these milestones, the game transitions into a 2D lunar environment where players must mine regolith, build a sustainable Moon base, assemble a rocket, synthesize fuel, and launch toward the Red Planet.

This project addresses the challenge of communicating complex space-exploration logistics through engaging, hands-on gameplay. Rather than passively reading about aerospace milestones, players actively solve the resource management and engineering hurdles required to use the Moon as a stepping stone to Mars.

It is important because interactive storytelling bridges the gap between technical space science and public inspiration, empowering a new generation to understand and envision humanity’s multi-planetary future.
details:
Zingularity: Artemis is a hybrid 3D/2D narrative and sandbox survival game inspired by NASA’s Artemis program and Terraria. The game begins in a 3D town of space enthusiasts where the protagonist interacts with family members, visits an observatory, and discovers a historical book about humanity’s journey from the Moon to Mars. Opening the book transitions gameplay into the protagonist’s imagination: a 2D side-scrolling sandbox set at the Lunar South Pole.

In the 2D phase, players manage four survival metrics—Oxygen, Radiation, Food, and Energy—while enduring solar radiation storms and meteorite showers. Players gather supply drops from Earth, mine lunar regolith, interact with astronaut NPCs, and feed materials into a Rocket Constructor Machine to assemble and fuel a spacecraft. After an animated trajectory sequence to Mars, players plant three flags (the United States, Ecuador, and a mission emblem) and construct a Martian base to complete the mission.

Benefits & Intended Impact The project translates complex aerospace concepts—such as In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU), radiation mitigation, and Moon-to-Mars mission staging—into accessible, hands-on gameplay. Its intended impact is to inspire students and general audiences to explore space science and recognize international participation in multi-planetary exploration.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software

  • Game Engine & Language: Godot Engine (GDScript).
  • Art & Level Design: Custom 2D pixel/sprite assets, multi-layer parallax backgrounds, and 3D environmental modeling.
  • Version Control & AI Assistance: Git/GitHub for workflow management, and LLMs (Claude) for ideation, structuring, and debugging.

Creativity & Factors Considered Rather than a purely technical simulator, the game blends a cozy 3D coming-of-age narrative with a Terraria-style 2D sandbox driven by a child's imagination. Our team grounded the gameplay in real NASA Lunar South Pole parameters (lower continuous radiation exposure) alongside dynamic space weather hazards and clear visual waypoints for an intuitive player experience.
